- Round to oval, multi-segmented conidia/spores attached at tips and bases
- Pale tan/beige coloration
- The conidia show internal divisions (multicellular)

Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch

Verticillium Wilt reference shows field symptoms, not microscopic. Moving to Alternaria.
Good match - Alternaria shows septate, segmented conidia similar to test image. Let me check Rhizopus.
Rhizopus shows dark sporangia - doesn't match. Checking Septoria.
Septoria is a leaf symptom image. Let me check Gray Mold (Botrytis) which has branched conidiophores with round conidia clusters.
Gray Mold shows clusters of small round single-celled conidia - partially similar structure but conidia differ. Let me check another Alternaria reference.

Excellent match! This Alternaria reference (Bugwood_3, 5505971) by Bruce Watt at 50μm scale shows nearly identical structures to the test image (5505973) - same branched septate conidiophores with oval multi-celled conidia. Very strong match. 

Must still cover remaining classes. Continuing:

I've now covered all 18 classes (19 reference views). The analysis is clear.

**Summary of findings:**
- Test image shows microscopic fungal structures: branched septate conidiophores with oval/round multi-celled conidia, 50μm scale, photographed by Bruce Watt
- **Alternaria Bugwood_3 (5505971)** is an almost perfect match: same photographer (Bruce Watt), same 50μm scale bar, identical septate branched conidiophores with oval multi-celled conidia attached at tips
- All other classes showed either field symptoms (leaf/fruit/stem/plant macroscopic views) or clearly different microscopic structures (Late Blight sporangia, Gray Mold single-cell conidia clusters, Rhizopus dark sporangia)
